title: Cop should have got Kuol data: Network profile was available to 911 dispatcher
article: A police officer who shot a Sudanese immigrant in a life-and- death struggle should have been armed with information about the violent history of Deng Fermino Kuol before walking alone into a potentially dangerous situation, a fatality inquiry heard Tuesday.

Kay Choi, a senior communications officer with the Calgary Police Service, said the 911 call taker should have been able to call up Kuol's checkered past on the local Police Information Management System, or the Canadian Police Information Centre's national database.
These programs would have been able to detail Kuol's criminal past, which included convictions for assault and drunk driving.
A warrant issued 11 days before Kuol's death would also have been available on the police networks.

"It would have been available on both (systems)," Choi told the inquiry, adding she had "no knowledge" of whether proper procedures were followed on Oct. 25, 2003, the day Const. Ira Macumber fatally shot Kuol after he attacked the officer with a knife.
It's not known whether the communications officer who took the initial call to 911 will take the witness stand today, the last scheduled day of the inquiry.
Macumber, however, testified earlier in the inquiry that he was given no information about the address or the person he was dispatched to check on.
Had he known, he would have handled the situation differently, he said.
"I would certainly take extra precautions by calling on backup and waiting for backup," Macumber told the court.
"I didn't have sufficient information in a timely manner before I got to this residence. I'm aware of what could have been done and what was done."
The two police databases also contained information about Kuol's attack on another Calgary police officer at the same address four months earlier.
Also on Tuesday, Kuol's best friend testified he called police the night of the shooting because he was scared of being evicted from his Forest Lawn apartment.
David Yall said that when Kuol showed up at the suite in the 1700 block of 37th Street S.E., he refused to let him in because Kuol was drunk and being too loud.
Yall's roommate, William Deng Dot, who was Kuol's uncle, had banned his nephew from the suite.
A drunk Kuol sat down outside Yall's apartment and refused to leave, occasionally banging on the door with his leg.
"He was not able to talk and he doesn't want to listen to me," Yall said through a Sudanese interpreter. "So I told him if this is the case, then I'm calling police."
Yall told the 911 call-taker he had a "big problem" at his apartment. He named "Deng Fermino" as the man who was causing the trouble.
Yall said he briefly spoke with Macumber after he arrived at the apartment. The officer, he testified, told him to go back to bed and he would take care of the situation.
A few minutes later, Yall heard two gunshots and rushed into the hallway to find his friend injured.
"He was calling the name of God and he was crying," Yall said of Macumber after the shooting. "Then he just screamed to 'Go inside. Go inside. Close the door.' "
Macumber testified last week that he was helping Kuol up a flight of stairs when the man turned around and tried to stab him in the chest.
The knife bounced off Macumber's body armour and slashed his bicep.
As the two men struggled on the stairs, Macumber was able to pull out his gun and fire two rounds.
Kuol was taken to hospital, where he died a short time later.
Yall said he did not see a knife near Kuol's body, or anywhere in the basement stairwell.
Police recovered a knife from the scene, but did not send it away for forensic testing.
